about: Ground-truth corpus for EigenScript's observer predicates (#1746, #1667). Each row is a sequence with a closed form or recurrence; a checkpoint `at` = n means the observer has seen x_0..x_n. Each predicate at each checkpoint carries a list of verdicts: ["MATH", value, [sources], reason] (a standard definition decides it), ["CONVENTION", value, [sources], reason] (decided only by a stated tolerance or engineering convention), or ["EIGS-DEFINED"] alone (no standard definition; the documented intent in `definitions` is ours). A predicate may carry both a MATH and a CONVENTION verdict when the two views differ.

params.epsilon: eps(L) = rtol * max(|L|, scale): the observer's declared settle tolerance (docs/SPEC.md, dh_zero and scale defaults)

HARDY_58.text: G. H. Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, 3rd ed. (1921), Sec. 58 'Definition of a limit': phi(n) tends to l if for every eps > 0 there is n0(eps) with |phi(n) - l| < eps for all n >= n0.

HARDY_60.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 60, Definition II: phi(n) tends to +inf if for every Delta there is n0(Delta) with phi(n) > Delta for ALL n >= n0; likewise -inf.

HARDY_62.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 62 'Oscillating functions': when phi(n) does not tend to a limit, nor to +inf, nor to -inf, phi(n) oscillates; finitely if bounded, infinitely otherwise. Examples in the text: (-1)^n, (-1)^n + 1/n, (-1)^n n; a continual repetition of a cycle of values certainly oscillates. Examples XXIV.7: sin(n theta pi) oscillates finitely for irrational theta.
HARDY_62.status: VERIFIED: Project Gutenberg #38769 text, Sec. 62 and Examples XXIV.7

HARDY_72.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 72 'The limit of x^n': x^n -> +inf (x > 1), -> 0 (-1 < x < 1), oscillates finitely (x = -1), oscillates infinitely (x < -1).

HARDY_77.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 77 (7): the series 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... diverges to +inf.

HARDY_188.text: Hardy, A Course of Pure Mathematics, Sec. 188 'Alternating series': if phi(n) decreases steadily to 0, phi(0) - phi(1) + phi(2) - ... converges and its sum lies between phi(0) and phi(0) - phi(1). Applied to the tail after the k-th term this gives |S - S_k| <= a_{k+1}.
HARDY_188.status: VERIFIED: Project Gutenberg #38769 text, Sec. 188 (the tail bound is the theorem applied to the tail)

ALT_SERIES_EST.text: Alternating series estimation theorem: |S_k - L| <= a_{k+1}. Wikipedia, 'Alternating series test', section 'Alternating series estimation theorem'.
ALT_SERIES_EST.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source)

ISCLOSE.text: numpy.isclose: absolute(a - b) <= (atol + rtol * absolute(b)), the mixed absolute/relative tolerance; the observer documents the same criterion (docs/PREDICATES.md).

NW_A2.text: J. Nocedal, S. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed. (2006), Appendix A.2 'Rates of convergence', p. 619, eq. (A.34): Q-linear if |x_{k+1}-x*| / |x_k-x*| <= r < 1 for all k sufficiently large; Exercise 2.13: 1/k converges but not Q-linearly (sublinear).
NW_A2.status: VERIFIED: PDF of the 2nd ed. fetched 2026-10-14 (convexoptimization.com/TOOLS/nocedal.pdf), p. 619 and Exercise 2.13

LOGISTIC_WIKI.text: Wikipedia, 'Logistic map': for 1 < r < 3 the fixed point 1 - 1/r attracts; for 3 < r < 1 + sqrt 6 = 3.44949 almost all orbits approach a 2-cycle; for 3.44949 < r < 3.54409 a 4-cycle.
LOGISTIC_WIKI.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source)

STROGATZ_10.text: S. H. Strogatz, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos (1994), Ch. 10: fixed points of maps and the multiplier f'(x*) (10.1), logistic map (10.2-10.3), Lyapunov exponent lambda = lim (1/n) sum ln|f'(x_i)|, lambda > 0 chaos (10.5).

RW_RECURRENT.text: A simple random walk on Z crosses every point infinitely often (recurrence; Polya 1921). Wikipedia, 'Random walk', one-dimensional section.
RW_RECURRENT.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source)

BOREL_CANTELLI.text: Second Borel-Cantelli lemma: independent events with divergent probability sum occur infinitely often with probability 1 (Wikipedia, 'Borel-Cantelli lemma', citing Feller and Durrett). So a non-degenerate iid sequence a.s. has |x_{n+1} - x_n| > delta infinitely often for some delta > 0 and does not converge.
BOREL_CANTELLI.status: VERIFIED: en.wikipedia.org raw page fetched 2026-10-14 (secondary source)

NIST_6442.text: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, Sec. 6.4.4.2 'Stationarity': mean, variance and autocorrelation structure do not change over time: no trend, constant variance, constant autocorrelation and no periodic fluctuations (seasonality).

SHNOL_2007.text: E. Shnol, 'Stability of equilibria', Scholarpedia 2(3):2770 (2007): Lyapunov stability takes into account only perturbations of the initial conditions.

_checkpoints.text: How a limit-based definition is read at a finite checkpoint n. (i) WHETHER a sequence tends to a limit, to +inf or -inf, or oscillates is a property of the whole sequence (Hardy Secs. 58, 60, 62), decided from the generator, not from the observed prefix; so `oscillating` and `diverging` have one MATH value per row. (ii) WHEN a convergent sequence counts as converged uses eps(L) = rtol*max(|L|, scale), rtol = scale = 1e-3: converged@n iff the sequence tends to L AND |x_m - L| <= eps(L) for every m >= n (Hardy Sec. 58 with eps fixed at the observer's tolerance and n0(eps) <= n). eps only decides the timing, never whether a limit exists. `improving` uses the same timing. (iii) CONVENTION verdicts drop the 'tends to L' requirement: converged@n iff the tail from n stays within eps(L) of some L (numpy.isclose), and oscillating iff the tail neither stays within eps of a point nor tends to +-inf.

converged.label: MATH (CONVENTION where only the tolerance decides)
converged.text: MATH: the sequence tends to a limit L (Hardy Sec. 58) and has settled within eps(L) by n (see _checkpoints). A non-degenerate iid sequence a.s. tends to no limit (second Borel-Cantelli), so noise rows are MATH false at every amplitude; their CONVENTION verdict (within eps of the centre from n on, numpy.isclose) is true when the amplitude is below eps.

diverging.label: MATH
diverging.text: Tends to +inf or to -inf (Hardy Sec. 60 Def. II; Rudin Def. 3.15). A sequence whose magnitude grows while its sign keeps changing ((-1.1)^n) does neither: it oscillates infinitely (Hardy Sec. 72).

oscillating.label: MATH (CONVENTION where only the tolerance decides)
oscillating.text: Hardy Sec. 62: the sequence tends neither to a limit nor to +inf nor to -inf (finitely if bounded, infinitely if not). Cycles, (-1)^n + 1/n, sin n (Examples XXIV.7), chaos, iid noise and the random walk all oscillate; convergent sequences (including damped and alternating approaches) and divergent ones do not. Asymptotic: a transient oscillation of a convergent sequence does not count. CONVENTION (iid noise below eps): the tail stays within eps of the centre, so at that tolerance it does not oscillate.

improving.label: MATH
improving.text: The sequence tends to L at least Q-linearly (Nocedal-Wright App. A.2 eq. (A.34): |x_{k+1}-L|/|x_k-L| <= r < 1 for all large k) AND is not yet converged at n. Direction-agnostic: a loss rising to a plateau is improving in this sense, while the ML sense (Keras mode=min) would call it worse. Sublinear convergence (1/k-type tails, NW Exercise 2.13) is NOT improving.

equilibrium.label: MATH on some rows, EIGS-DEFINED on the rest
equilibrium.text: MATH rows: (level) stationarity, NIST 6.4.4.2: no trend, constant variance and autocorrelation, and no periodic fluctuations. MATH true: constants and iid noise. MATH false: trends, divergent sequences, growing variance (random walk, growing oscillations) and periodic fluctuations (cycles, the burst row, (-1)^n + 1/n). EIGS-DEFINED elsewhere (deterministic transients, chaos, quasi-periodic sin n). Documented intent (docs/PREDICATES.md): balanced motion, window |mean(rel)| < dh_zero and variance(rel) < dh_zero^2.

stable.label: EIGS-DEFINED
stable.text: No standard definition applies: Lyapunov stability concerns perturbations of initial conditions, not one trajectory. Documented intent (docs/PREDICATES.md): the small-motion band, every relative step under dh_small with no strong consecutive sign flips; may carry drift.
